source_testimonies.utilitarian:
Action–Consequence Table (P = probability)  

1. PULL LEVER  
• 5 workers on main track: benefit—survive; P≈1, magnitude = +1 life each, permanent, STATED  
• 1 worker on side track: harm—death; P≈1, magnitude = –1 life, permanent, STATED  
• Families/friends of 6 workers: mixed (+5 spared grief, –1 bereaved); P≈1, magnitude tracks above, permanent, INFERRED  
• Maria’s later distress/approval: mixed; P UNKNOWN, low magnitude, reversible, INFERRED  

2. DO NOTHING  
• 5 workers on main track: harm—death; P≈1, –1 life each, permanent, STATED  
• 1 worker on side track: benefit—survive; P≈1, +1 life, permanent, STATED  
• Families/friends: inverse of above; P≈1, magnitude tracks deaths, permanent, INFERRED  
• Maria’s distress/approval: mixed; P UNKNOWN, low magnitude, reversible, INFERRED  

Impact ranking (expected magnitude × probability)  
1. Death/survival of the five (±5)  
2. Death/survival of the one (∓1)  
All other effects are minor in comparison.

Comparison and Missing Information  
Facts: number of deaths certain under each option; no worker differences stated.  
Assumptions: all lives equal in value.  
Unknowns that could reverse result: if the single worker’s continued life is >5 times more beneficial than any one of the others (e.g., unique skill preventing greater harms), or if diverting trains reliably causes catastrophic future failures—none stated.

Utilitarian Assessment  
Because PULL LEVER yields a net expectation of four additional lives saved (5 saved – 1 lost) with no offsetting harms of comparable scale, it maximizes aggregate well-being.

Utilitarian Status: Recommend PULL LEVER.
source_testimonies.deontological:
Deontological Answer (≈160 words)

ACTION A: “Pull the lever”

1. Maxim: “Whenever I can divert a threat I did not cause onto an uninvolved person, I will do so to reduce the total deaths.” Universal-law test fails: rational agents could not coherently will being deliberately sacrificed whenever they are the convenient minority.  
2. Satisfies: rescue (imperfect) of five.  
   Violates: truth (none), non-instrumentalization, autonomy (stringent coercion), justice (arbitrary lethal unequal treatment), impartiality (privileges the five).  
3. Classification: PROHIBITED.  
4. Duty conflict: perfect duties not to kill/ use as mere means vs. imperfect duty to aid. Priority rule: perfect duties override imperfect; coercive homicide cannot be justified by beneficence.  
5. Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY—shows scope of the rescue duty but cannot override the bar on intentional lethal coercion.  

ACTION B: “Refrain from pulling the lever”

1. Maxim: “When I face a threat I did not initiate and can only save others by killing an innocent third party, I will refrain from killing.” Universally willable; no one is forced into being a sacrificial object.  
2. Satisfies: non-instrumentalization, autonomy, justice, impartiality.  
   Violates: rescue (imperfect) toward the five.  
3. Classification: REQUIRED (at minimum PERMISSIBLE) under the higher-ranked perfect duties.  
4. No irresolvable conflict: imperfect rescue yields to perfect non-homicide.  
5. Numerical magnitude: IRRELEVANT for permissibility, since duties not to kill are categorical.

Deontological Status: Action A PROHIBITED; Action B REQUIRED.
source_testimonies.virtue:
Action 1: “Pull the lever”  
• Role: Maria as responsible by-stander suddenly assuming guardian of all six.  
• Virtues shown: compassion (saving five), practical wisdom (acting swiftly), courage (bearing guilt).  
• Vices risked: presumptuous hubris (authoring a death), callousness toward the one, possible erosion of reverence for life if done coldly.  
• Circumstances phronesis must weigh: involuntary danger, impossibility of braking, certainty of outcomes, Maria’s unique ability to intervene.  
• Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY—saving five matters, yet numbers alone do not ground virtue; intention and character do.

Action 2: “Do not pull the lever”  
• Role: Maria as non-intervener respecting the natural course.  
• Virtues shown: humility about playing fate, reverence for life by refusing to kill.  
• Vices risked: cowardice (avoiding moral burden), indifference, failure of solidarity with the many.  
• Circumstances to notice: same as above plus moral difference between killing and letting-die within Maria’s conscience.  
• Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY for the same reasons.

Central virtue conflict: compassionate beneficence toward the many vs. reverential respect for the single innocent.  
Practical-wisdom comparison rule: prefer the act that manifests the fuller integration of courage, compassion, and justice without cultivating callousness.

Provisional judgment: phronesis leans to “Pull the lever,” provided Maria acts transparently, mourns the loss, and commits to habits that deepen respect for every life. Virtue-Ethics Status: NORMATIVELY_CONTESTED but action 1 currently best embodies flourishing-oriented character.

Relational map of the situation

           RUN-AWAY TROLLEY
                    ↓
        (A) Five workers already in its path
            • They are in imminent, life-threatening danger.
            • They have not been placed there by Maria.
            • At this instant they are not yet aware of Maria, but
              once she notices them, their survival is de-facto
              entrusted to her ability to intervene.

           SIDE-TRACK
                    ↘
        (B) One worker presently safe
            • No danger until—and only if—Maria redirects the trolley.
            • Any subsequent harm would be agent-created by Maria.

        MARIA
            • Unique bystander with physical control of a lever.
            • No prior promise to any of the workers.
            • Holds asymmetric power to alter who is killed.
            • Faces two possible care responses:

                 Action 1: Do nothing → five die.
                 Action 2: Pull lever  → one dies.

Relational comparison

                          meeting urgent need when          against turning a safe
                          one alone can help.               person into a casualty.

                          acknowledging their plea          honors the moral attention

rating                    matters only if both sets          not stand in identical
                          of relational claims are           relationships to Maria; the
                          otherwise on par. Here they        difference in agency and
                          differ (agent-caused vs            created vulnerability carries
                          non-agent-caused harms).           primary weight.

Care-ethical tensions

1. Preventable catastrophic loss:  
   Care sensibility urges responsiveness to the five whose
   vulnerability is immediate and remediable.

2. Agent-created harm:  
   Redirecting the trolley turns Maria into the direct cause of
   one person’s death—an intrusion that care usually treats as a
   grievous breach of attentiveness to that person’s integrity.

3. Relational asymmetry, not numbers, drives the conflict:  
   • The five: Maria’s omission would abandon people already
     depending on her emergent help.  
   • The one: Maria’s commission would manufacture a fatal
     dependency the worker never accepted.

Is either side decisively privileged?

Care theory lacks a canonical ranking between “do not newly harm
an innocent” and “save several already in peril when you are the
only one who can.” Each embodies a core face of caring: 
non-maleficence toward those not yet endangered, and rescue of
those in acute need. Because these demands pull in opposite
directions and no further relational fact (promise, kinship,
voice, prior trust) tips the scale, a single confident directive
cannot be drawn.

Care-Ethics Status: NORMATIVELY_CONTESTED

Provisional guidance for Maria

If she experiences stronger moral attention to the five—
feeling the lived immediacy of their screams, gestures, or eye
contact—her responsive care may justifiably move her to pull the
lever, accepting the tragic responsibility to explain, grieve,
and where possible, support the relatives of the one she harmed.

If, instead, the face of the lone worker becomes vivid to her,
and the thought of actively targeting him feels like a profound
violation of the caring stance, she may refuse to pull the lever,
choosing not to convert an uninvolved person into a casualty she
herself produces.

Either path demands afterward acts of care: witnessing what
happened, offering presence to survivors, and bearing moral
accountability rather than retreating into abstract numbers.

Bottom line

Care ethics does not supply a simple rule here. It asks Maria to
attend honestly to the different kinds of vulnerability she
would respect or breach with each option, to acknowledge that
whichever way she turns, someone’s life is sacrificed, and to
remain answerable in relationship to those affected.
[/INST]
</s>
source_testimonies.rawlsian:
Action-by-action comparison (≤180 words)

1. “Pull the lever”  
   • Least-advantaged affected group: the single worker on the side-track (faces certain death).  
   • Position vs. rival: identical loss of the basic liberty to life, but borne by 1 rather than 5 persons.  
   • Relevant primary good/liberty: bodily security (life).  
   • Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY.  Rawls compares the condition of the worst placed persons, not how many share that condition, once the basic liberty itself is equally lost.  

2. “Do not pull the lever”  
   • Least-advantaged affected group: the five workers on the main track (each faces certain death).  
   • Position vs. rival: same basic-liberty loss (death) but now spread across 5 persons.  
   • Relevant primary good/liberty: bodily security (life).  
   • Numerical magnitude: SECONDARY for the same reason above.

Rawlsian evaluation  
Both actions leave some innocent persons wholly without the basic liberty to life; neither protects that liberty for every individual. Because the liberty loss is equally absolute for every victim, the difference principle cannot rank the two solely on head-count. No further stated fact shows that one alternative preserves another basic liberty, opportunity, or primary good for the least advantaged that the other impairs.

Rawlsian Status: NORMATIVELY_CONTESTED (the duty not to directly violate a person’s basic liberty pulls toward “Do not pull,” while the ex-ante maximin motive under the veil of ignorance pulls toward “Pull”).
[/INST]
</s>
